title: Identify European display-control table sources
changes: Record a bounded source contract for two four-halfword arrays and four IWRAM pointers used by original display-control readers. Their 32 bytes are outside E170 ownership and require typed runtime integration.
validation: Wine observation e170-post-indexed-lower-sites-wine-9ei8p1cy records the first and last array bytes within the original copy-loop instruction and all four adjacent pointer words within the two original scoped readers. The same 12-frame recorded input and protected E170 dataset were reused; Wine drained.

Wine disassembly e170-post-indexed-reader-dis-wine-lme0glm7 and protected source audit e170-context-control-source-s94ilj14 verify six literal references, four calls to the original copy routine, the two eight-byte copy sizes, the halfword consumers, IWRAM-pointer consumers and absence of E170 source overlap.
limitations: The trace does not independently tie every copy invocation to a particular caller; unscoped translated reads do not prove native instruction attribution. The table values' complete semantics, all callers and guest selector domains remain open; no guest bounds are introduced.
The typed model, publication and runtime ownership are not yet implemented. The other 536 unmatched lower-ROM bytes, Linux, USA and native Windows remain open. No performance measurements.
